title: Permanent tripartite dialogue turns worker and employer voice into a labour-governance institution, but ownership determines whether it becomes operative
source_unit: ILO report on the Kurdistan Region of Iraq Social Dialogue Forum, published September 3, 2026
geography: Kurdistan Region of Iraq, with exchange links to Federal Iraq and wider Arab States social-dialogue practice

observations.period: September 1-3, 2026; establishment of the Social Dialogue Forum

denominator.unit: tripartite constituent groups: government, workers, employers

institutional_status.value: A permanent tripartite platform was launched to address labour-market challenges and shape policies affecting the world of work

representation.value: The Founding Document establishes equal representation of government, workers, and employers in both the Forum and its Secretariat

dialogue_scope.value: The Forum is tasked with consultation, information exchange, cooperation, labour legislation, workers' rights, trade-union freedoms, labour-market policy, and international labour standards

observations.method: Official ILO institutional announcement describing the founding document, constituent representation, mandate, and support arrangement; it is not an evaluation of Forum performance.
observations.uncertainty: The Forum is newly established. The source does not show meeting frequency, agenda outcomes, worker coverage, policy adoption, enforcement, budget, or whether equal representation produces equal influence.
observations.subgroup: Kurdistan Regional Government, worker organizations, employer organizations, trade unions, enterprises, and workers affected by labour and socio-economic policy.
observations.counterinterpretation: A formal tripartite body can legitimate pre-existing power or become consultative without changing decisions; equal seats do not guarantee equal resources, information, access, or bargaining power.

implementation_followup.value: The Forum is intended to review labour legislation and follow up on its implementation, rather than only discuss policy design

working_committees.value: The Founding Document allows specialized committees on labour legislation, social security, employment, occupational safety and health, and other member-defined priorities

action_test.value: The launch explicitly frames the challenge as translating dialogue into action and continuous engagement

observations.method: Official ILO report of the Forum's mandate and stated implementation ambitions; no outcome observation or counterfactual is available.
observations.uncertainty: The source provides no evidence yet about committee formation, legislative change, compliance, occupational safety, social-security access, or dispute resolution.
observations.subgroup: Workers and employers affected by legislation, social security, employment policy, safety and health rules, and labour-market transitions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Adding committees and consultation can increase procedural time without improving decisions; implementation follow-up may also be constrained by fragmented authority or political conflict.

observations.period: September 2026; external support and institutional ownership

denominator.unit: EU-funded ILO BEIT project supporting the Forum

external_support.value: The Forum's establishment was supported through the ILO Building Equitable and Inclusive Transformation project funded by the European Union

technical_support.value: The ILO will continue technical expertise, capacity development, and learning support while priorities and direction remain with tripartite members

durability_condition.value: The source identifies member ownership and continued engagement by government, workers' organizations, and employers as conditions of sustainability

observations.method: Official partnership and institutional-formation announcement; it reports the support architecture and stated durability condition but not long-run financing or organizational behavior.
observations.uncertainty: The Forum's sustainability, autonomy, funding, membership breadth, and relationship to federal and regional authority remain untested.
observations.subgroup: Tripartite members, EU and ILO support institutions, Federal Iraq observers, regional policy actors, and workers and firms affected by future decisions.
observations.counterinterpretation: External support can supply expertise and convening power but may create dependence or an institution whose legitimacy is associated with donors rather than local constituents.

related_sources.claim: ILO project page for the BEIT support project referenced in the Forum announcement.

boundary: This record captures the institutional design and stated durability conditions of a new tripartite labour-governance forum. It does not establish effective representation, policy influence, enforcement, worker outcomes, social-security access, or institutional survival.
